catalog.summary: Searchable dialog of commands and destinations.

patternStatus: The combobox pattern with a listbox popup answers the search field and the list: DOM focus stays on the input and the list is navigated with aria-activedescendant, which is the pattern's own note. The popup never closes on its own — the list is the surface — so aria-expanded is always true, recorded as a departure The dialog pattern is answered by the dialog family this one composes. Both read on 2026-09-15.

nativeElement.reason: As combobox records it: a datalist is drawn by the operating system and cannot hold a group, a description, a shortcut or a disabled option. The input itself is kept — a real input with the browser's caret, selection, IME and text editing.

composedFamilies.dialog: the layer, the scrim, presence, portal, focus containment and restoration, Escape and outside press, the single z-index stack. Composed as upload-viewer composes it: React wraps the panel in Dialog with surface plain and placement top; Angular projects it into sl-dialog. Nothing of the layer is redrawn.
composedFamilies.kbd: the legends of every shortcut, on an item and in a footer hint, through Shortcut with variant plain. The family writes the notation once and kbd resolves it for the reader's platform.
composedFamilies.highlight: the mark on the run the query found, as combobox draws it.
composedFamilies.spinner: the ring that stands in for the search glyph while loading.
composedFamilies.skeleton: the three rows the list shows while loading with nothing to show.

collection.reason: docs/component-features.md §5 makes the ranking an adapter with a default. The default scores label and keywords with the collator createFilter already builds, at base sensitivity, so an item cannot pass the ranker and show no mark. Four strengths — whole label, prefix, word start, substring — and a keyword one step below them. The typeahead module the scope named is a prefix matcher with a reset window and a cycle; it does not score, and it is not this.

keys.reason: menu announces aria-keyshortcuts and never fires one; this family has to fire one, the hotkey that opens it. The matcher decides what mod means on the reader's platform and refuses a modifier the shortcut did not ask for. isEditableTarget is where a shortcut without a modifier stays quiet, which is what §5 asks of a global shortcut.

presentation.dialog: the family composes dialog: a modal layer at the top of the viewport, opened by the trigger, the hotkey or the handle, closed by Escape, the scrim, an executed item or the handle
presentation.inline: the root is written where the consumer put it, with no layer: inside a popover, a drawer or a page. It is the answer menu gave when it refused the filtered menu — a list filtered by typing is a combobox by role, and this is that surface without a dialog around it.

highlight.focus: stays on the input for the whole interaction
highlight.reason: The pattern's own note, and the model combobox already uses. The input must keep focus for the reader to type.

items.shape: id, label, keywords, description, group, icon, shortcut, meta, disabled, href, onSelect, children
items.data: Items are values, not children: the ranker scores label and keywords, and a family that read the DOM would rank what it had just painted (cmdk reads textContent). renderItem in React and an ng-template in Angular substitute the item's content; the option element and its wiring are the family's.
items.href: an item with href renders as an anchor with role option; Enter follows it and a modified Enter is left to the browser
items.children: an item with children opens a page whose items are the children; the item carries data-page and draws the arrow part
items.disabled: kept in the list, announced with aria-disabled, skipped by every movement key, never highlighted by the pointer and never executed

ranking.default: createRanker().rank over label and keywords, locale-sensitive at base sensitivity
ranking.off: rank={null}, for a list the consumer has already ranked on a server
ranking.order: with a query: within a group by score, then by the consumer's order; groups by their best item. Without a query: the consumer's order, groups in the order of the groups prop, ungrouped items last.
ranking.highlight: matchRanges on the label, and the match part that marks what it found
ranking.limit: limit caps the rows drawn; it is a product decision and not virtualization

pages.open: an item with children: Enter or the pointer pushes its id onto pages, clears the query and highlights the first child
pages.trail: the pages part lists every open page as a page button; pressing one returns to it
pages.back: Backspace with an empty query, and Escape with an empty query, pop one page before anything closes
pages.async: children may arrive later: the consumer replaces items and the family finds the page by id again
pages.reason: cmdk leaves pages to the consumer's own state and kbar navigates by parent; Raycast and Linear draw the trail and return on Backspace. The stack is state a consumer can own, so it has a model.

recent.shown: with an empty query, at the root page, when recent holds at least one id that names an item: a first group labelled by the recent message, in the order of the array
recent.updated: executing an item asks onRecentChange with the id moved to the front and the array cut at recentLimit
recent.unknown: an id that names no item is not drawn and is kept in the array
recent.persist: the product's: it receives the array and stores it
recent.reason: VS Code, Raycast and Linear open on recents; no surveyed library ships them. Filed under queue, the word toast put in the vocabulary for an ordered collection the family holds and trims and the consumer may own.

execution.event: onSelect(item, request) on the root and onSelect on the item; reason pointer or keyboard, the source event, keepOpen() and the pending promise
execution.async: a handler that returns a promise keeps the palette open, marks the item data-loading and aria-busy, and refuses to execute the same item again until it settles; on fulfilment the palette closes unless keepOpen() was called; on rejection it stays open and the status row announces the error message
execution.close: closeOnSelect closes with reason select after a synchronous handler and after a fulfilled promise
execution.reason: docs/process/build-order.md: 'async actions' and 'does not run a disabled item'.

hotkey.listener: keydown on the document, capture phase, preventDefault when it matches
hotkey.editable: a shortcut without a modifier does not fire inside an editable target; a chord with one fires anywhere
hotkey.open: when the palette is already open the hotkey focuses the input and selects the query instead of closing; toggle() on the handle closes
hotkey.reason: Mantine defaults to mod+K, React Aria's example opens on ⌘J, and Linear, Slack, GitHub and Vercel all answer ⌘K. Firefox uses it for its search bar and preventDefault wins.

busy.reason: While an answer is travelling the header shows the ring where the search glyph was, as combobox shows it where the chevron was.

placeholder.reason: The list waits as three rows the height of an item rather than as one sentence. It is hidden from assistive technology: the status row is the live region.

mark.reason: As combobox records it: the span a query found is the `highlight` family inside this family's label part, from the same collator the ranker used.

announce.count: the count message, a plural on {count}, after every change of the result set
announce.error: the error message, with {message} filled, after a rejected handler
announce.reason: docs/process/build-order.md: 'announces the number of results through the live-announcer'. The row is visually hidden and never duplicated: the announcer refuses to say the same sentence twice in a row.

wiring.role: combobox on the input, listbox on the list, option on each item, group on each group, separator between groups, status on the live region
wiring.aria-expanded: true, always: the list is the surface and never closes on its own
wiring.aria-activedescendant: the input names the highlighted item, and nothing while there is none
wiring.aria-selected: true on the highlighted item, false on every other, because the pattern says selection follows focus in the listbox and the palette has no other selection
wiring.aria-busy: on the list while loading, on an item while its handler is pending
wiring.aria-keyshortcuts: on an item with a shortcut, as menu writes it: Meta+K for mod+k on a Mac, Control+K elsewhere; a sequence is drawn and not announced
wiring.aria-labelledby: on each group, naming its group-label
wiring.aria-label: the input message on the input; the label message on the dialog's content, through the dialog family
wiring.aria-hidden: on shortcut, meta, arrow, search, busy, placeholder and the footer hints: each is drawn for the eye and said another way
wiring.autocomplete: off on the input, with spellcheck false
wiring.tabindex: -1 on clear; the page buttons in the trail keep their place in the tab sequence
wiring.data-page: on an item that opens a page
wiring.data-empty: on the root while the list holds nothing
wiring.data-query: on the root while the query is not empty

keyboard.effect: moves the highlight to the next item, wrapping when loop is true
keyboard.focus: stays on the input, and the caret does not move

keyboard.effect: moves the highlight to the previous item, wrapping when loop is true
executes the highlighted item; with children, opens its page; with href, follows it. With no highlight, nothing. A disabled item is never highlighted and never executed.
keyboard.focus: the input, or wherever the executed item sent it

keyboard.effect: with a query, clears it; with a page open and no query, returns one page; otherwise closes the palette, which is the dialog's Escape. In inline presentation the last step does not exist. The pattern's optional clearing of the combobox is the first step.
keyboard.focus: the input, or the trigger once the palette has closed

keyboard.effect: the browser's caret movement, never intercepted, which is the pattern's editable branch
keyboard.focus: the input, caret at the first character

keyboard.effect: the browser's caret movement, never intercepted
keyboard.focus: the input, caret after the last character

keyboard.effect: moves the highlight ten items on, or to the last, and never wraps. Optional in the pattern for a grid popup; adopted as combobox adopted it.
moves the highlight ten items back, or to the first, and never wraps
the browser's caret movement, never intercepted
the browser's caret movement, never intercepted
the browser's text editing, never intercepted while the query holds text. With an empty query and a page open, returns one page, which is what Raycast and cmdk do.
the browser's text editing, never intercepted
typed into the input, which ranks the collection. Never intercepted.
inside the dialog, the layer's focus containment: the trail's page buttons are reachable and clear is not. Inline, focus leaves the family.
opens the palette from anywhere in the document; already open, focuses the input and selects the query

focus.onOpen: the input, through the dialog's initial focus; the highlight goes to the first enabled item when autoHighlight is set and to nothing otherwise
focus.contained: by the dialog family while presentation is dialog
focus.restore: to the trigger by the dialog family; inline, focus never left the input
focus.disabledItems: announced with aria-disabled, carry data-disabled, keep their place and are skipped by every movement key
focus.removal: a query that removes the highlighted item moves the highlight to the first enabled item with autoHighlight, and to nothing without it

responsive.below: description and meta are hidden; the shortcut stays; the trail keeps one page and truncates
responsive.reason: The panel answers its own inline size, which is the dialog's measure or the popover's. Rule 4 of docs/token-foundation.md: the breakpoint is a literal.

motion.highlight: none: the current row does not transition, because a change of row is a reading and not a movement
motion.reason: Only the layer arrives and leaves. A transition on the highlight lags behind a reader holding ArrowDown.

closeAtEveryWidth.reason: The dialog closes on Escape and on the scrim, and a ✕ beside a search field reads as clear, so above the dialog's full-screen step there is no close part. Below it there is no scrim to press and a touch screen has no Escape, which left a palette opened by mistake with nothing to press but a command: close is a word — the close message — at the end of the field, drawn by the stylesheet under the dialog's own full-screen query alone, and it asks open to be false with the reason dismiss. A consumer with outsidePress none above the step still draws its own in the footer.

itemShortcuts.reason: Shortcuts on items are drawn and announced, never bound. kbd says 'does not register shortcuts on its own', and a global registry is a family of its own. The consumer binds one with matchesShortcut in three lines, shown on both reference pages.

prefixModes.reason: Modes by prefix (> # /) are composition: onQueryChange reads the first character and the consumer swaps items. Shown on both reference pages.

virtualization.reason: As menu and select defer it. limit and a scrolling list cover the palette until then.

checkedItems.reason: A palette executes; it does not toggle. menuitemcheckbox belongs to menu.

vimBindings.reason: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+P and Ctrl+J belong to the browser and the platform; the pattern does not list them. A consumer binds them on the input's own keydown.

debounce.reason: As combobox declines it: the consumer debounces the fetch.
